issues.legal_issue: A landholder’s entitlement to a ryotwari patta for qualifying lands requires actual cultivation, not merely an intention to cultivate or resume cultivation.
material_facts: The landholder claimed a ryotwari patta for land that had never been occupied by a ryot.

The governing provision required the landholder to have cultivated the land personally or through servants or hired labour from the specified date and to have been in direct and continuous possession from that date.
The landholder purchased the land after the specified date and said he reclaimed it after purchasing it.
The Assistant Settlement Officer and Tribunal found that the landholder had failed to prove cultivation from the specified date.
issues.conclusion: The statutory requirement of having cultivated the land is not satisfied by showing only an intention to cultivate or resume cultivation. The order rejecting the patta claim was restored.
issues.legal_principle: Section 13(b)(iii) of the Madras Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act, 1948 requires actual cultivation by the landholder, the landholder’s servants or hired labour, as well as direct and continuous possession from the specified date. The words “has cultivated” do not encompass a mere intention to cultivate. The Court distinguished the Madras Full Bench decision in Periannan v. A.S. Amman Kovil, which construed Section 3(10) of the Madras Estates Land Act, 1908, and relied on its construction of that provision in Chidambaram Chettiar v. Santhanaramaswami Odayar, while holding that the express language of Section 13(b)(iii) controls.

predicates.ryotwari_pattta_claim: A landholder seeks a ryotwari patta for land under a statutory scheme governing conversion of an estate to ryotwari tenure.
predicates.qualifying_unoccupied_land: The land is of the kind for which the claimed patta depends on it having been abandoned or relinquished by a ryot, or never having been occupied by a ryot.
predicates.intention_without_actual_cultivation: The landholder shows an intention to cultivate or resume cultivation but does not prove actual cultivation by the landholder, servants or hired labour from the required date.

issues.definition: When a landholder claims a patta for qualifying unoccupied land but establishes only an intention to cultivate and not actual cultivation from the required date, the cultivation requirement is not met.

issues.legal_issue: Objectors to a ryotwari patta claim who participated in the tribunal proceedings may be made parties to a supervisory revision concerning that claim even if they were not initially impleaded.
material_facts: The appellants objected to the landholder’s patta claim before the Settlement Officer.
The Tribunal disposed of the landholder’s appeal after hearing the appellants, although they had not been impleaded as parties to that appeal.
The appellants were not impleaded in the High Court revision concerning the patta claim, but the High Court heard them on whether the landholder was entitled to the patta.
issues.conclusion: The appellants were entitled to be made parties to the revision concerning the patta claim, and the Court proceeded to hear their appeal on the merits.
issues.legal_principle: The Court reasoned from the appellants’ status as objectors to the patta application and their participation in the Tribunal proceedings: they might properly have been parties to the landholder’s Tribunal appeal and were entitled to be made parties to the related High Court revision. No earlier case or specific statutory provision was relied on for this procedural conclusion.

predicates.patta_claim_revision: A supervisory revision concerns a tribunal decision on a landholder’s patta claim.
predicates.objected_to_original_claim: A person objected to the landholder’s patta claim before the original decision-maker.
predicates.heard_in_tribunal: The tribunal heard that person while deciding an appeal concerning the patta claim.

issues.definition: When a person objected to a patta claim and was heard in the tribunal proceedings, that person is entitled to be a party to a supervisory revision concerning the claim.
